chunks: He created the earth and suspended it without being busy, retained it without support, made it stand without legs, raised it without pillars, protected it against bendings and curvings and defended it against crumbling and splitting (into parts). He fixed mountains on it like stumps, solidified its rocks, caused its streams to flow and opened wide its valleys. Whatever He made did not suffer from any flow, and whatever He strengthened did not show any weakness.
ai.seo_question: How does Nahj al-Balagha describe the creation and stability of the earth?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) articulates the concept of divine stability (istiqrar) by highlighting that the earth was anchored not by physical pillars but by God's direct will, a theme resonating with Shia theological discussions on God's absolute self-sufficiency (Ghani) versus the contingency of creation. The description of mountains as 'pegs' (awtad) serves as a cosmological sign of God's power to maintain order without external support, reinforcing the belief in Tawhid as the foundation of both spiritual and physical reality. This imagery invites reflection on how divine power sustains the universe continuously, rather than merely initiating it and leaving it to natural laws.
